papers.csv.title: Riemannian-Geometric Fingerprints of Generative Models
papers.csv.venue: IEEE/CVF International Conference on Computer Vision
papers.csv.venue_name: IEEE/CVF International Conference on Computer Vision
papers.csv.raw_venue: Proceedings of the IEEE/CVF International Conference on Computer Vision
papers.csv.abstract: This work defines artifacts and fingerprints of generative models using Riemannian geometry, presents a gradient-based algorithm for computing them from generated samples, and evaluates source-model attribution across four datasets, 27 model architectures, and vision and vision-language modalities.

papers.csv.title: A Rich Knowledge Space for Scalable Deepfake Detection
papers.csv.authors: Inho Jung, Hyeongjun Choi, Binh M. Le, Hohyun Na, Simon S. Woo
papers.csv.abstract: The paper introduces the 3.6-million-image MMI-DD facial deepfake collection and SD² detector. A separate general synthetic-image experiment trains a Stable Diffusion 1.4 versus ImageNet probe and evaluates eight GenImage generators, demonstrating transfer beyond facial manipulation.

papers.csv.title: Conditional Uncertainty-Aware Political Deepfake Detection with Stochastic Convolutional Neural Networks
papers.csv.abstract: This study evaluates deterministic and stochastic CNN inference for binary political-image classification on 2,000 authentic photographs and 2,000 AI-generated images selected from OpenFake, including controlled in-distribution and generator-disjoint out-of-distribution analysis.

papers.csv.title: Detecting Violent Deepfakes: Dataset and a Compact Attention Network with Multi-Scale Supervision
papers.csv.authors: Surbhi Raj, Jimson Mathew, Arijit Mondal
papers.csv.abstract: The paper introduces DVID, with 17,442 Stable Diffusion violent-scene images and 17,253 real images, and a compact attention detector reporting 98% accuracy and 97.8% average precision, with additional cross-diffusion-model and color robustness tests.

papers.csv.title: Abductive Corroboration of Probabilistic AI Models for Forensic Synthetic Media Detection
papers.csv.abstract: The study evaluates three passive synthetic-image classifiers on 2,000 GPT-Image-2 and 2,000 real Flickr images and measures how agreement among independent classifiers changes false-positive and true-positive performance. A separate SynthID experiment is not required for the passive results.

papers.csv.title: SPARK-IL: Spectral Retrieval-Augmented RAG for Knowledge-Driven Deepfake Detection via Incremental Learning
papers.csv.authors: Hessen Bougueffa Eutamene, Abdellah Zakaria Sellam, Abdelmalik Taleb-Ahmed, Abdenour Hadid
papers.csv.abstract: SPARK-IL combines dual-path spectral representations, retrieval-augmented classification, and incremental learning. On UniversalFakeDetect it evaluates 19 GAN, face-swap, low-level, perceptual, and diffusion generators and reports 94.60% mean accuracy.

papers.csv.title: Deep Learning for CGI and Visual Forgery Detection: A Comprehensive Survey
papers.csv.venue: International Journal of Data Science and Analytics
papers.csv.raw_venue: International Journal of Data Science and Analytics
papers.csv.abstract: This survey organizes deep-learning methods for CGI and visual-forgery detection across architectures, spatial/spectral/color representations, and multimodal fusion, with substantive coverage of modern GAN and diffusion detection, CIFAKE, GenImage, ArtiFact, and cross-generator generalization.

papers.csv.title: Learning Counterfactually Decoupled Attention for Open-World Model Attribution

papers.csv.venue: IEEE/CVF International Conference on Computer Vision

papers.csv.raw_venue: Proceedings of the IEEE/CVF International Conference on Computer Vision
papers.csv.abstract: CDAL learns counterfactually decoupled attention for passive open-world source-model attribution. Experiments cover OW-DFA facial attacks and the broader OSMA GAN benchmark with real images, 14 seen source classes, and 53 unseen source classes.

papers.csv.title: Language-Guided Hierarchical Fine-Grained Image Forgery Detection and Localization
papers.csv.authors: Xiao Guo, Xiaohong Liu, Iacopo Masi, Xiaoming Liu
papers.csv.abstract: HiFi-Net++ unifies image-level forgery detection and pixel-level localization across CNN/diffusion synthesis, facial manipulation, and conventional editing. The paper constructs HiFi-IFDL and separately evaluates general synthetic-image detection across ProGAN and 18 held-out generation methods.

decision.decisive_evidence: The abstract and experiments introduce DVID with 17,442 Stable Diffusion violent-scene images and 17,253 real images, report 98% accuracy and 97.8% average precision, and independently test cross-model/color robustness on DiffusionForensics.
decision.narrowed_scope_rationale: The paper detects fully generated still-image scenes and is not restricted to face or identity manipulation.
decision.identity_note: DOI, OpenAlex, normalized title, DVID acronym, and exclusion checks are clear. A 2024 paper by the same authors has a different title, venue, DOI, and contribution.

proposals.title: Abductive Corroboration of Probabilistic AI Models for Forensic Synthetic Media Detection
proposals.abstract: The study evaluates three passive synthetic-image classifiers on 2,000 GPT-Image-2 and 2,000 real Flickr images and measures how agreement among independent classifiers changes false-positive and true-positive performance. A separate SynthID experiment is not required for the passive results.
proposals.version_note: The current authoritative form is arXiv 2607.05434; no later formal publication was established.

affiliations.raw: The Alan Turing Institute, Defence and National Security Programme, London, United Kingdom

proposals.original_title: Abductive Corroboration of Probabilistic AI Models for Forensic Synthetic Media Detection
proposals.exact_unresolved_question: Is there a separable, independently evaluated passive synthetic-image forensic method or passive-detector analysis that remains valid without SynthID or any watermark recovery? Identify the watermark-free results.

decision.decisive_evidence: Section III defines three passive image classifiers applied independently to 4,000 images. Table III reports their standalone results, and Table VIII reports watermark-free corroboration: two-classifier agreement lowers false-positive rate from 20.7% to 1.7%, while three-classifier agreement yields 0% observed false positives. SynthID is confined to a separate 400-image experiment.
decision.narrowed_scope_rationale: The passive detector analysis and corroboration remain valid without watermark recovery.
decision.identity_note: No strong identifier, normalized-title, author/year/venue, method/acronym, or active-exclusion match; bounded fuzzy results are unrelated.

proposals.title: SPARK-IL: Spectral Retrieval-Augmented RAG for Knowledge-Driven Deepfake Detection via Incremental Learning
proposals.abstract: SPARK-IL combines dual-path spectral representations, retrieval-augmented classification, and incremental learning. On UniversalFakeDetect it evaluates 19 GAN, face-swap, low-level, perceptual, and diffusion generators and reports 94.60% mean accuracy.
proposals.version_note: The Springer ICPR proceedings chapter, published in the 2027 volume, is canonical; arXiv 2604.03833 is its preprint version.

proposals.title: Learning Counterfactually Decoupled Attention for Open-World Model Attribution
proposals.venue: Proceedings of the IEEE/CVF International Conference on Computer Vision
proposals.abstract: CDAL learns counterfactually decoupled attention for passive open-world source-model attribution. Experiments cover OW-DFA facial attacks and the broader OSMA GAN benchmark with real images, 14 seen source classes, and 53 unseen source classes.
proposals.version_note: The ICCV 2025 proceedings paper is canonical; arXiv 2506.23074 is its preprint version.
proposals.original_title: Learning Counterfactually Decoupled Attention for Open-World Model Attribution
proposals.exact_unresolved_question: Do CDAL’s open-world attribution benchmarks use naturally occurring image-generation traces to identify source generators beyond pure facial-manipulation attribution? Verify inputs, source labels and absence of injected signatures.

decision.decisive_evidence: Section 2 distinguishes active injected fingerprints from passive attribution and identifies CDAL as passive. Section 4/Table 3 evaluates OSMA source labels over real images, 14 seen GAN classes, and 53 unseen GAN classes; OSMA includes ImageNet, LSUN, COCO, and Yosemite content beyond faces, while OW-DFA supplies face-swap and other generative-editing attacks.
decision.narrowed_scope_rationale: CDAL attributes source generators from inherent visual traces and includes a substantive non-face benchmark without injected signatures.
decision.identity_note: DOI, arXiv, OpenAlex, normalized title, CDAL acronym, author/year/venue, and active-exclusion checks found no current representation.

proposals.title: Language-Guided Hierarchical Fine-Grained Image Forgery Detection and Localization
proposals.abstract: HiFi-Net++ unifies image-level forgery detection and pixel-level localization across CNN/diffusion synthesis, facial manipulation, and conventional editing. The paper constructs HiFi-IFDL and separately evaluates general synthetic-image detection across ProGAN and 18 held-out generation methods.
proposals.version_note: The International Journal of Computer Vision article is canonical; arXiv 2410.23556 is its preprint version.

proposals.original_title: Language-Guided Hierarchical Fine-Grained Image Forgery Detection and Localization
proposals.exact_unresolved_question: Does the proposed unified detector independently evaluate the CNN-synthesized image domain as a substantive AI-image forensic task? The saved abstract stops before its method and evaluation.

decision.decisive_evidence: Sections 4–5 construct the 13-method, 100,000-images-per-method HiFi-IFDL benchmark spanning fully synthetic and partial images. Section 5.4 independently trains a ProGAN detector and tests 18 methods including Stable Diffusion, Sora, Midjourney, DALL·E 3, and InstantID while the main system evaluates image detection and localization.
decision.narrowed_scope_rationale: CNN/diffusion-synthesized image detection is a substantive independent task within the unified detection/localization contribution.
